claims.text: The as-cast Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is single phase.
The as-cast alloy has a nominally uniform microstructure immediately after casting.
Rapid annealing produces a state with minimal short-range chemical order.
Slow cooling near the stability limit enhances local chemical ordering.
The proposed treatment sets can differ primarily in SRO while retaining identical grain sizes.
Atom probe tomography can quantitatively measure the relevant SRO and local atomic clustering.
Enhanced SRO increases local dislocation pinning.
Increased local dislocation pinning raises yield strength.
Minimal SRO facilitates easier dislocation nucleation.
Minimal SRO facilitates easier dislocation movement.
Under identical dynamic loading, slowly cooled samples with greater SRO will have higher yield strength than rapidly annealed samples.
Under identical dynamic loading, slowly cooled samples with greater SRO will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than rapidly annealed samples.
The proposed SRO-controlled behavior applies from 200 to 600 K.
The proposed behavior applies only at strain rates that do not themselves induce additional microstructural changes.
Other deformation mechanisms may dominate outside the stated temperature and strain-rate regime.
The rapidly annealed, minimally ordered condition is the experimental baseline.
Failure to observe statistically significant yield-strength and strain-rate-sensitivity differences correlated with measured SRO differences would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field says that disappearance of mobility differences when SRO levels are similar would falsify the SRO effect, although equal behavior at equal SRO is consistent with that effect. The formal falsification rule instead, and more appropriately, requires no mechanical differences despite confirmed SRO differences.
